# CratonBench v1

Four tests, frozen before any model exists. A test's data and metric never change; a better test gets a new ID. Each is fingerprinted: the hash of its definition, its metric and every test file, and the ratchet refuses a run whose fingerprint differs.

Region `central_italy`, data snapshot `96a163f798d8f9cc`.

## What is held out

| Held out | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| Era A | 2016-08-24 | 2018-01-01 |
| Era B | 2009-01-01 | 2010-01-01 |

And 29 GNSS stations, one in ten, chosen by a salted hash among stations with at least two years of data, three visible neighbours within 50 km, and no day-to-day jump over 1 m: `AT03`, `AT08`, `AT10`, `ATMI`, `AZRA`, `BAR2`, `BENE`, `CADG`, `CAMU`, `CIPV`, `FRES`, `MRRA`, `MUR1`, `OVRA`, `PAVO`, `PESR`, `PIET`, `PIG3`, `RETO`, `ROU3`, `RSM1`, `SGRE`, `SUBL`, `SULM`, `TRIV`, `UNOV`, `VCAH`, `VCRA`, `VTRA`.

## CB-01 · Geo-perplexity

Hide 15% of the measurements in the two held-out eras and ask for each one back. A quake's time and magnitude type are shown; where it was, how deep and how big are hidden. A GNSS day shows the station and its site to 0.01°; its east, north and up are hidden. Every answer is a probability distribution, scored in bits on fixed bins, like perplexity for a language model. The tide token computed at a hidden quake is hidden too, because it sits at the quake's epicentre.

- **Metric:** bits per masked token, mean over instruments (lower is better)
- **Fingerprint:** `faa360aee280f001`
- **Test data:** queries 28,000 · seismic catalog 17,310 · gnss daily 10,690 · hidden tides 17,310

| Instrument | Channel | Bin width | Edges |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seismic_catalog` | lat | 0.01 | k·w |
| `seismic_catalog` | lon | 0.01 | k·w |
| `seismic_catalog` | depth_km | 1 | k·w |
| `seismic_catalog` | magnitude | 0.1 | k·w − 0.05 |
| `gnss_daily` | east | 0.001 | k·w |
| `gnss_daily` | north | 0.001 | k·w |
| `gnss_daily` | up | 0.001 | k·w |

## CB-02 · Apennines 2016-17 forecast

A forecast every midnight for the next day: how many quakes in every 0.1° cell and every 0.1 magnitude bin, knowing only the quakes before midnight. 494 days of the Amatrice-Visso-Norcia-Campotosto sequence. Models fit only on data before 24 August 2016. Scored by the joint Poisson log-likelihood per M3+ quake, the CSEP standard; the difference between two models is their information gain.

- **Metric:** log-likelihood per earthquake (bits), M≥3, daily 0.1° forecasts (higher is better)
- **Fingerprint:** `4186dd5479fe6163`
- **Test data:** days 494 · M>=3 1,065 · M>=1.5 42,807 · magnitude types ML 42,381, Md 291, Mw 135 · largest 6.5

## CB-03 · L'Aquila 2009 era holdout

The same game for 2009, the year of L'Aquila, with models fitted only on data before 2009. The catalogue before 2005 is in another magnitude type (Md), so the baselines fit on four years, 2005 to 2008.

- **Metric:** log-likelihood per earthquake (bits), M≥3, daily 0.1° forecasts (higher is better)
- **Fingerprint:** `a12a2e1ceb896ad1`
- **Test data:** days 365 · M>=3 315 · M>=1.5 11,070 · magnitude types ML 10,492, Md 510, Mw 68 · largest 6.1

## CB-04 · GPS gap-fill

Hide every day of 29 GNSS stations from everything, then rebuild their daily positions from the other stations. A station's series starts from an arbitrary origin, so each station's mean offset per component is removed before the RMSE.

- **Metric:** RMSE (mm), hidden stations, offset per station and component removed (lower is better)
- **Fingerprint:** `9449170471e9295c`
- **Test data:** stations 29 · station days 86,373

## CB-15 · Efficiency

What the model's pretraining run cost on the RTX 2060: model FLOPs utilisation, the share of the GPU's peak the run actually used (6N + 12·L·H·Q·T FLOPs per token, against 25.8 TFLOP/s of fp16 tensor-core math). A run that needs more than 6 GiB of VRAM can't be scored at all. Tokens per second, peak VRAM and minutes ride along.

- **Metric:** model FLOPs utilisation (%) of the pretraining run, inside 6 GiB of VRAM (higher is better)
- **Fingerprint:** `284cb4cd3a09a0a9`
- **Test data:** budget gib 6.0

## CB-09 · Two planets

CB-02's calendar and scoring on six simulated planets where the truth is known. Three ETAS planets, where Italy's own fitted ETAS makes the quakes: nothing beats the truth on average, so a forecaster has to tie it. Three physics planets (Dieterich rate-and-state seismicity on Apennine-shaped faults, stress transfer with shadows, a hidden fluid source), where ETAS is the wrong model and a forecaster has to beat it. Seed k scores planet k of each kind. The gap column is the sim-to-real gap: the mean factor off the real Apennines, in doublings, over the five statistics.

- **Metric:** bits per M3+ quake on the physics planet, daily 0.1° forecasts (higher is better)
- **Fingerprint:** `2e0396974965f7d7`

| Catalogue | Seed | quakes per day | b value | busiest 1pct days share | busiest 5pct cells share | daily count cv | gap | test M3+ |

## Add a method

Implement the task's protocol (`MaskedPredictor`, `Forecaster`, `GapFiller` or `EfficiencyReport` in `craton/bench/tasks.py`), register it with `register_method`, and run `craton bench run NAME`. The run lands in `results/pending/`; `craton ratchet --accept` puts it on the scoreboard if nothing got worse.
